      RESEARCH PROGRAM
      From forecasts to operators, with decisions as the test.
      My doctoral work linked forecasting, uncertainty representation, and constrained optimization in coupled water–energy systems. I extend the same principle to neural operators: learn distributed physical dynamics, then evaluate the model through the control action, feasible design, or operating decision it changes.
    
    
      
        Doctoral foundation
        Decision-focused forecasting
        Probabilistic predictions are trained and evaluated through the schedules, costs, and constraints they induce in coupled water–energy systems.
      
      
        Method extension
        Neural operators for distributed dynamics
        I study function-to-function models that map initial conditions, geometry, boundary conditions, and forcing terms to spatiotemporal solution fields.
      
      
        Decision criterion
        Operator-based control and optimization
        I examine how rollout error, gradient error, and constraint violation alter closed-loop actions and optimized designs.
      
      
        Physical testbed
        Materials processes
        Field-evolving materials processes provide a concrete setting for experiment selection, process control, and constrained design with learned solution maps.

title: Urban water forecasting and pressure modeling
text:
Daily urban water-demand forecasts can attain low average error while responding late when demand changes direction. This lag reduces their value for planning the next operating period.
The knowledge-based bi-correction model addresses the problem in two stages. Lag-penalty attention extracts prior sequence and feature information associated with timely demand changes. A stacked LSTM produces the primary forecast. A masked weighted Markov chain then corrects selected residuals using posterior error information.

title: Urban water forecasting and pressure modeling
text:
Trend-sensitive evaluation
The study introduces mean prediction trend effectiveness to test whether a model follows changes in demand more closely than a naive forecast. Reporting this metric alongside absolute-error measures separates response timing from average numerical accuracy.

title: Urban water forecasting and pressure modeling
text:
Pressure under unobserved variation
CritiCoder considers macroscopic pressure when measured inputs do not explain every disturbance in a water distribution system. Its Coder models the response associated with observed variables, while the Critic changes the loss so that the remaining pressure variation can be represented as an uncertain disturbance.
The comparison tests whether CritiCoder’s error increases less than conventional regression error at nodes more strongly affected by unobserved disturbances.

The program began with decision-focused forecasting and constrained optimization for coupled water–energy systems and now extends to neural operators for distributed dynamics, control, and materials processes.

title: Research
text: My research asks how learned models of physical systems can support decisions under dynamics, uncertainty, and constraints. The program began with decision-focused forecasting and constrained optimization for coupled water–energy systems and now extends to neural operators for distributed dynamics, control, and materials processes.

title: Research
text:
Decision-focused forecasting and constrained optimization
During my doctoral research, I treated a predictor as part of a decision pipeline rather than an endpoint. Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize trains probabilistic electricity-cost forecasts through the stochastic water-supply schedules they induce. A differentiable upper bound on downstream optimality gap passes a decision-relevant signal back to the predictor.
Companion work on lag-free demand forecasting and uncertain pressure regression addressed when a prediction error occurs and which unobserved effects it represents. Together, these studies shifted evaluation from aggregate forecast accuracy to decision sensitivity, operating cost, and constraint satisfaction.

title: Research
text:
From predictors to neural operators
Neural operators extend this question from finite-dimensional time series to maps between physical fields. The model class changes, but the research criterion remains the same: a surrogate is useful when it preserves the control or optimization decision that matters.
I study operators that map initial conditions, geometry, boundary conditions, and forcing fields to spatiotemporal solutions. Field error is one diagnostic; rollout stability, gradient quality, control cost, and feasibility determine whether the learned map is suitable for downstream use.

title: Research
text:
Neural operators in downstream control
A learned solution operator can supply state rollouts to a controller without solving the governing equations from scratch at every control step. I quantify how local approximation error accumulates over a control horizon and changes the selected action. This relation motivates training objectives that account for closed-loop behavior as well as field reconstruction.

title: Research
text:
Neural operators in constrained optimization
Embedding a differentiable neural operator in an optimization problem links physical field prediction to design or operating decisions. Gradient accuracy and feasibility indicate whether the surrogate can be used inside the optimizer. Decision sensitivity shows when a small field error produces a materially different optimum.

title: Research
section: Materials processes as a physical testbed
text:
Materials processes as a physical testbed
I am extending this framework to materials processes, where the state evolves as a field over space and time. These systems provide a concrete setting for testing whether learned solution maps can support experiment selection, process control, and constrained design.

title: Research
text:
Related work on generated actions
A related collaborative thread examines learned action generation in physical environments. DRIFT stores local LiDAR geometry as graph memory during recurrent diffusion, extending the broader interest in models whose outputs must satisfy geometric and decision constraints.

title: Water-energy resource scheduling
text:
Urban water supply consumes electricity throughout treatment, transport, and distribution. The resulting schedule depends on the expected electricity cost, while errors in that forecast can change operating cost and the selected schedule.
The study models the full water-supply process as a stochastic scheduling problem with uncertain electricity prices. Forecast quality is evaluated both by pointwise prediction error and by the objective value of the induced schedule.

title: Water-energy resource scheduling
text:
Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize
Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize combines a probabilistic forecasting model with the downstream stochastic program. Its forecast distribution supplies uncertain cost parameters to the scheduler, and the resulting schedule defines the decision loss used to update the predictor.
Direct differentiation through this optimization problem is difficult. SPTO+ replaces the exact optimality gap with a differentiable convex upper bound derived from Lagrangian duality. The bound supplies a surrogate gradient while retaining the scheduling problem in the training objective.

title: Water-energy resource scheduling
text:
Evaluation
Experiments on real-world water-supply systems compare forecast quality, operating cost, and decision regret. SPTO reports lower operating cost and regret than the tested two-stage forecasting and optimization baselines.
